name: squiid
desc: Do advanced algebraic and RPN calculations
why: An RPN and algebraic calculator in the terminal; RPN is an old-school environment with a bit of character.

brief.what_it_is: Squiid is a terminal calculator written in Rust that supports both RPN (reverse Polish notation) and algebraic input, with a simple terminal user interface built on Ratatui. The homepage describes it as a modular calculator and the successor to the author's earlier ImaginaryInfinity Calculator. From the homepage alone I could not see the exact inputs or outputs beyond calculations typed into the terminal UI.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Squiid as the successor to the authors' previous ImaginaryInfinity Calculator, so it continues that earlier project rather than starting from a stated new problem.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says Squiid is modular and will support plugins in the future, but it does not explain the internal mechanism. The README and documentation were not reachable, so the mechanism is unknown.
brief.install_notes: The homepage has a 'Download Squiid' link, but I could not resolve its target. The brew description gives no further setup, and I saw no runtime, account, or configuration requirements. The source code and documentation links on the homepage also had no resolvable URLs in the fetched text, so I could not follow them.
brief.standout: It is a Rust terminal calculator that handles both RPN and algebraic entry in one tool, which is a niche combination. The scout note frames RPN as an old-school environment with some character.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has no release date or changelog, and the GitHub repository I guessed returned 404 under two capitalisations. I could not confirm the source location, last commit, or last release.
brief.caveats: Plugin support is listed as something that 'will be added in the future', so it is not available yet. I could not reach the source code or documentation, so the feature list rests only on the short homepage. The brew caveats field is empty. I found no stated platform or licence information.
